WARNING- very long rant. Conciseness is not a strength I possess.

Now, I've lurked on this subverse for a little while as I find gives me an outlet for my fustration over our culture of of complacency, mediocrity and politcal correctness and "acceptance" to the point of insanity. I have, untill now, refrained from making an account or posting as I don't necessarily agree with every belief espoused here and don't think my hatred is on the same level as most of you guys- but that's neither here nor there. After reading so many posts about the incompetency and laziness of fat nurses I just felt like I finally needed to vent about this and get it off my chest (pun intended). I hope you guys will be open to it as this was very cathartic for me to write out after all these years.

When I was 17, few years ago, I underwent open heart surgery. I was fortunate enough to have the procedure done at a very prestigious hospital by a doctor who is number one in the world for that type of surgery. My experience with all of the nurses was amazing- since I was a young kid in the adult unit, and never bothered them or complained they tended to dote on me and give me special treatment and extra attention. All except one nurse; and you guessed- she was obese.

When I was being transferred from ICU to the Post-OP unit they brought in a handful of nurses to assist to with the move, and see to last minute care like removal of my chest tubes. One of these nurses was the fatty in question- a morbidly obese woman maybe in her late 30's (it's always hard to tell though when they have so much extra weight). While the other lovely nurses were preparing my gurney that would move me to the other floor, this woman decides to sit her fat ass down and strike up a conversation with me. Now, I was only maybe 24-30 hours out of surgery. They had only taken my repsirator out maybe 12 hours prior. I could hardly speak at all and my body (and my mind) was still in shock at having undergone the ordeal that is major surgery. All of the other nurses were sensitive to this and kept their dialogue with me very brief, exchanging questions and pleasantries that only required one word answers on my part. But this fucking bitch.

She started out by asking me what age I was- I was able to force out a labored and whispery "17". Then she goes "Oh! A senior, my daughter is a senior! Are you going to prom? My daughter is, we were picking out her dress..."- blah, blah don't remember, don't care, but it went on. When she finally stopped I just shook my head, and forced out another whispery response. Now at first I thought she was maybe just trying to cheer me up, but at this point her face changed and she actually looked offended and annoyed that I (a day out of open heart surgery) was not enganging in her asinine conversation, and she goes "No? Well why not?" and some drivel about it being an important memory to not miss out on and blah, blah- this time in a markedly bitchier tone. Now, not only was I exhausted and in pain, and not only was I just physically incapable of enganging her questions the way she clearly was expecting me to, but the subject she was discussing was also bringing up some painful feelings for me. I had only made the first two months of my senior year, as a very close family member had died suddenly and unexpectedly that Fall, and I had been with them when it happened. Now, just a few months later here I was lying in a hospital bed. Senior prom was not even on the bottom list of my priorites, but not a priority at all (I wouldn't even be recovered in time to go). For a long time I struggled with feeling like a "freak", because while most other teens were busy playing sports, and going out partying and whatever teens do I was dealing with illness and death, and sitting in hospitals and wakes. I felt ashamed of having this condition, and felt as though it made me inferior to others. So anyway, I became upset and started to tear up a little as she was going on and on about senior proms, and her daughter's fucking dress (major surgery has a tendency to lead to a period of depression, so I was already quite emotional). When she finished and paused for me to respond I just kind of mumbled and turned away. At that she actually became visibly pissed off and proceeded to roll her eyes, huff and get up out of her seat to assist the other nurses with.. yanno, doing their job.

Now THIS- this is the worst part. All that other stuff I could, at the time, placed down to ignorance and inexperience, and I couldn't have expected all of the nurses to know my situation; but this is the thing that to this day makes me rage when I think about it. This is the thing that pretty much concluded for me, without a doubt, that my thoughts about so many fat people being immature, lazy, stupid and incompentent were not at all unfounded.

So, she stands up and goes to get something on a stand on the other side of my bed from where she was. However, instead of walking around my bed to retrieve it, this lazy sack of shit decides to LEAN OVER ME to get it. Now, being the size that she was and clearly having no perception of her own body, she proceeds to lean the weight of her massive fat chest/breasts directly on top of MY CHEST- yanno the thing that was just split wide open hours prior and currently filled with tubes and being held together with wire and sutures.

Waking up from surgery, the first thing I remember is the feeling of immense weight and pressure as if there were a 200lb person sitting directly on top of my chest; and that feeling remained for weeks after the surgery. So now in addition to that feeling, I have an actual person of that size (probably larger) pressing the weight of their massive chest on my 100lb frame. Thank God her feet were still planted on the floor so as not to be placing her entire weight on top of me- if that were the case I would have been seriously injured. The few seconds that she was on top of me felt like minutes and I felt all the air being forced out of me as well as shooting pain in my abdomen where she was pressing on my chest tubes. I wasn't able to cry out until she got off of me, and when she did I let out a terrible wail- which in itself caused me even more pain. She looked at me and, quickly realizing what she had done, turned red and looked over at the nurses to see if they were looking. Unfortunately they hadn't seen the incident as they were busy preparing for my move, but were now looking after hearing my cry. She looks at them, looks at me, and in her standard bitchy, indifferent affectation goes "What? What's the matter?" without an ounce of compassion or concern. "You're hurting me!" was all I managed to force out. She replied, almost condescendingly, with "Oh stop it, you're fine. You have your button. Press your button" (button being the morphine drip- you press a button to release a dose into your IV) and turned away from me. No apology, no checking to see if I was hurt- nothing but concern over whether the other nurses witnessed her utter stupidity and incompetency. I was in so much pain later that night that my nurse ended up needing to order me a shot of Dilauded as the morphine just wasn't cutting it. Fortunately, after my move to Post OP floor, I never saw that nurse again.

I wish I would have spoken up and said something, but I was so painfully shy back then I never did. Since then, I have countless other stories and examples of the incompetency and laziness of fat nurses (and other fat professionals), but this is probably the worst I have ever encountered as this woman could have very well caused me serious injury. My one solace is in the thought that she probably didn't work there for very long. The nurses who work in that hospital, on that floor especially, do not fuck around. They have some of the best work ethic and bedside manner of any nurses I've ever been in the care of. I got to know some of them fairly well during my stay (and during the stay of another family member previously). Some of them would stay on for well over 12 hours, eating rarely and with no sleep. Oftentimes they'd walk around drenched in sweat from the exertion of running all over the hospital for hours on end seeing to the various insistent needs of their patients- and always with warmth and compassion. There's no way a fat waste like that woman could possibly keep up with the demands of a job like that.
